verdict.tagline: Endless digging and crafting, provided you survive the confusing start.
for_you_if: you enjoy deep crafting and exploring vast worlds
you want to play cooperative multiplayer with friends
you love discovering massive amounts of content
not_for_you_if: you dislike relying on external guides
you want clear tutorials in the early game
you find initial survival mechanics overwhelming

Neat and interesting!
This game definitely falls into a category of game where to properly enjoy it, you must either have a comprehensive understanding of the game or be actively reading along with the Wiki.
As a new player jumping in alongside more experienced friends, and expecting a similar progression to Minecraft, I found myself very quickly lost and overwhelmed. 
Beyond basic crafting i began struggling to acquire items, i found myself quickly being left in the dust by other players who began to acquire jetpacks and yo-yos, and then the boss's started coming and i was little more than greasy smear after that. 
I tried again on my own but began hitting walls in my progress and eventually grew frustrated and bored. 
Maybe its the friends who introduced me, but mostly it feels like the game.

Terraria is very good, the boss fights are unique and challenging, the variety of classes and weapons is fun to choose from, your next move is unpredictable; the enemies and challenges thrown at you can make the game so much more interesting and entertaining to survive in. I would recommend having the wiki or google open next to you because things can get a little confusing at times, also be prepared to deal with grinding and probably rage LMAO. Anyways, great game, would 100%  recommend.

-also, Empress of light is fit as ♥♥♥♥ bro, would crack frfr

One of the most fun survival games out there. Thousands of items and random stuff to do, a ton of bosses to fight, and really fun building mechanics that goes really well with the 2D perspective of the game. It definitely rivals Minecraft as one of the best.

There are only a couple of problems with the game though.

The entire game before you beat the wall of flesh boss is absolutely miserable and really boring to play, which is why most players would quit at that point before reaching the mechanical bosses. After that the game is perfect.

The game also really falls off a cliff after you beat moon-lord. You realise you can still fight duke fishron and daytime of empress of light, but they are no challenge if you have the zenith or the endgame gear you get from moon-lord. At that point nothing really feels worth your while.

That's where the main problem comes in. Terraria is just not playable enough. The reason why games like Minecraft are still so popular today is because even after you kill the ender dragon, there are still challenges to face. With terraria, you end up becoming an unstoppable god and nothing makes you feel challenged. Stuff that could fix this is adding new dimensions to the game you can explore, with enemies that will always match your level. Maybe even new bosses that take place after moon-lord, or a new game plus mechanic where your world's boss accomplishments become reset, and enemies can hit harder than master mode meaning you will have to take full advantage of farms and other stuff. Apart from that..

Progression is extremely satisfying, weapons and armour are all unique and are tied to their own classes, absolutely TONS of unique blocks to build with, and the bosses in this game are terrifying for sure.

Yeah I'll shut the ♥♥♥♥ up though. You'll like this game. Buy it.

Get past the fear of complexity and the game's mechanics start feeling natural after the first few hours. Don't be afraid to look up the wiki when you get stuck, like I initially did. There are certain things you just can't figure out by yourself without excessive experimentation and an unreasonable amount of time.

As for the game's quality, it's almost like trying to sell you Minecraft. It's good, you already know it's good, you're just too scared because it's harder and more complex than Minecraft.

Terraria is one of the greatest video games ever created because it gives players complete freedom while constantly rewarding creativity, exploration, and skill. Unlike many games that become repetitive after only a few hours, Terraria continues to introduce new enemies, weapons, bosses, and mechanics throughout the entire playthrough. Every cave has the potential to hide rare loot, every biome feels unique, and every boss victory unlocks exciting new content. Whether someone enjoys building incredible structures, fighting difficult enemies, or collecting every item in the game, Terraria offers something for everyone. Few games manage to balance freedom and progression as perfectly as Terraria does.

One of Terraria's biggest strengths is its incredible amount of content. Even the base game contains thousands of items, dozens of bosses, and countless hours of exploration. Every class—melee, ranged, magic, and summoner—provides a completely different way to experience the game, encouraging players to start new worlds and experiment with different playstyles. The progression feels incredibly satisfying because every boss defeated opens the door to stronger equipment and new challenges. Instead of feeling repetitive, every stage of the game feels fresh and rewarding.

Terraria also stands out because of its outstanding replay value. No two worlds are exactly the same, meaning every new adventure brings different terrain, structures, and treasures. On top of that, different difficulty modes completely change the experience by adding tougher enemies, smarter bosses, and better rewards. Once players finish the base game, they can dive into an enormous collection of community-made mods like Calamity, Infernum, and Thorium, each adding enough content to rival entire games. The nearly endless amount of replayability makes Terraria a game that players can enjoy for years without running out of things to do.

When I first got this game, I thought it was just going to be a 2D Minecraft. 
WRONG.

This game, with such little size, keeps you busy for days, months, even YEARS!
Every time I want to play a game and I don't have a lot of storage, or don't want to wait forever for a game to download; I play Terraria.

Such an incredible game, and the tmodloader found on steam which introduces mods and more content to the game, as well as quality of life mods makes it even better. If you have the money, buy this game.

Been playing this game for over 10+ years across multiple devices and keep coming back. I've been a fan of this game and its community, devs, mods, content, you name it. Genuinely may be my top game of all time, especially so due to the amazing work of the devs and the ever growing communities love for this game, which is much well deserved. The game scams itself by only being $10 and I would gladly pay more for this game then i ever would for a triple-A title, as is evident in me buying the game 6+ times over the years. This game and its ♥♥♥♥♥♥ but funny RNG. The hellish hours you have to spend grinding for things and building arena's that take forever. I wouldn't have it any other way. Thank you Terraria and the amazing devs and community for making and continuing to make this game some of the best media i've ever been and will be apart of. Godspeed to Terraria, I will continue to love this game and its mods for a long time.

More than 10 years later it is still one of my favorite games. Super fun to play, even more with friends. You'll end up hating them a bit because they will mess up the order in the chests for sure though.

The graphics are old but still cute. It still gets updates, contents, and a lot of mods that add gameplay and creatures too. I played for +200 hours and i still see myself playing more.

10/10 recommended, you get a lot of fun for a super cheap price and can even get the 4 copies pack for less than 30€!

Good game. Had fun solo and with friends, mostly with friends. Has lots of content, fun gameplay and modded content is just insane, literally insane. I got this for sale, so its a really good value for money for me. already finished this game like 4-5 times and still want to play more. Very much recommended if you can get it on sales. This game is fun for both solo and team gamers.
